licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: Despina sings “Che rumor, che canto è questo!” with the four lovers (the libretto gives it to the lovers, with romor), vò, “io vò guardar” the second time, tornaro (the libretto has tornano), “Gli sposi vostri…” and “Lo sposo mio…” with the libretto's ellipsis (printed “...”), and “Ma se li veggono” (Despina and Don Alfonso) beside “Ma se ci veggono” (Ferrando and Guglielmo).

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 334–340, bars 290–371 of No. 31
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the No. 31 Finale (671 bars) read in fourteen page ranges, sung lines and piano each by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the zoomed page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by eight fresh proofreaders (pages 332–338 clean). The German singing translation is left out. All the singers of this section have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out; singers who do not sing in this section are left out. The soldiers' chorus off stage (sopranos, altos, tenors and basses) has a staff for each part and is heard with the piano; it has no role here. Where the print gives the basses no words, they sing the tenors' words. Cut from the one-file finale at bars 290–371: from the Maestoso (D major), as the soldiers' chorus is heard off stage, to the end of the Allegro before the Andante. No new time signature is printed at the Maestoso, so alla breve goes on; the Allegro from bar 21 is in 3/4, and alla breve again from bar 67. The sopranos and altos print “mol-to c do-man” in bar 8 (the tenors and basses “mol-to e”); it is kept as printed. Playback tempo: Maestoso at ♩ = 90, then Allegro from bar 21 at ♩ = 128, from René Jacobs's recording (harmonia mundi), 2:28.
